questions.q: A person has limited shoulder movement because the joint structure prioritises stability and the surrounding tissues are tight. Which statement best explains their flexibility?
options: Flexibility is unaffected by joint structure.
Both joint structure and the resting length of surrounding tissues can limit range of movement.
Only aerobic power determines joint range.
Muscular strength always increases flexibility.
questions.feedback: Flexibility is influenced by joint structure and by the length and elasticity of muscles, ligaments and surrounding tissues.

questions.q: Which situation best demonstrates meaningful representation rather than token representation?
options: A woman is appointed but excluded from major decisions.
A committee advertises its diversity while women hold positions but remain excluded from funding decisions.
One leadership position is created without any responsibilities.
Women hold leadership roles and have genuine influence over decisions about funding, facilities and policy.
questions.feedback: Representation is meaningful when people have genuine influence over decisions, not simply when they occupy a position.

questions.kk: Prevalence and Trends of Physical Activity, Physical Inactivity and Sedentary Behaviour
questions.q: Data: adults aged 65+ — 33.4% met the guidelines; 40.7% participated in daily physical activity. Which conclusion is supported?
options: Everyone who reported daily physical activity must also have met every component of the physical activity guidelines.
Daily activity was less common than meeting the guidelines.
Some older adults were active daily without necessarily meeting every guideline requirement.
No older adults were regularly active.
questions.feedback: Daily participation and overall guideline compliance are different measures, so daily activity does not guarantee all requirements were met.

questions.kk: Assessment of Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour
questions.q: What is a major limitation of a recall survey?
options: It cannot be used with large participant groups
Participants may forget or inaccurately report previous activity.
It cannot collect information about sedentary behaviour.
It always requires expensive wearable technology.
questions.feedback: Recall error and inaccurate self-report are important limitations of recall surveys.

questions.q: How can diverse athlete representation support inclusion?
options: It guarantees equal funding for every sport because broader representation automatically produces identical sponsorship and media investment across all competitions.
It can help viewers see people like themselves participating and strengthen a sense of belonging.
It removes transport barriers.
It ensures every viewer becomes physically active.
questions.feedback: Seeing diverse athletes represented respectfully can challenge stereotypes and help more people feel that participation is possible and welcoming.

questions.q: A rural athlete must travel several hours and pay substantial fees to receive specialist rehabilitation. This most directly demonstrates:
options: a geographic and financial access barrier.
improved inclusion.
psychological skill development.
safer officiating.
questions.feedback: Cost and location can restrict access to appropriate recovery support.

questions.q: How can gender stereotypes influence sporting participation?
options: They can shape beliefs about which sports or roles are suitable for particular genders.
They guarantee that athletes choose sports that match their abilities.
They affect leadership but not participation.
They only influence professional sport.
questions.feedback: Gender stereotypes can affect confidence, aspirations, support and perceptions of belonging, which may influence sporting choices and participation.

questions.q: Which activity is an example of transportation?
options: Walking from home to a train station
Completing a structured circuit class at a local gym
Gardening in a backyard
Playing a social card-based movement game
questions.feedback: Transportation involves physical movement used to travel from one location to another.

questions.q: An academy records the following observations over four weeks: Week 1—moderate workload, low fatigue; Week 2—moderate workload, low fatigue; Week 3—high workload, high fatigue; Week 4—high workload, reduced enjoyment and concentration. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: High workload always causes poor mental health.
The athlete should stop training permanently.
Increased workload was associated with greater fatigue and reduced enjoyment and concentration in this case.
Training workload cannot influence mental fitness.
questions.feedback: The pattern shows an association in this case but does not prove that workload is the only influence.

questions.q: Which statement best explains sleep optimisation?
options: Reducing sleep so more time is available for training.
Using habits and opportunities that support sufficient, good-quality sleep.
Sleeping for exactly the same number of hours as every other athlete.
Replacing recovery activities with daytime naps.
questions.feedback: Sleep optimisation involves creating conditions and routines that support adequate sleep quality and duration.
